trust_decision.summary: Whether a <use> element counts as a reference is decided in the pre-pass Resolver::collect(), which runs on the raw attribute names; the sanitizer's own later attribute cleaning rewrites any case variant of href/xlink:href to the canonical name, so the sanitizer is the thing that makes the reference live. The graph must therefore decide on the same case-insensitive view of the attribute name as that normalization, not on XPath's case-sensitive @href test.

landing_point.why: the advisory summary names Resolver::processReferences and its case-sensitive '[@href or @xlink:href]' XPath predicate, which is the only line the report points at

fix_sites.entry_point: Sanitizer::sanitize() (src/Sanitizer.php:216) reaches it at src/Sanitizer.php:246; the bundled CLI src/svg-scanner.php:131 calls the same method

Same public entry point Sanitizer::sanitize() (src/Sanitizer.php:216), which reaches the helper from Resolver::processReferences (src/ElementReference/Resolver.php:109), Resolver::determineInvalidSubjects (src/ElementReference/Resolver.php:132), Sanitizer::isUseTagDirty (src/Sanitizer.php:669) and Sanitizer::isUseTagExceedingThreshold (src/Sanitizer.php:687)
fix_sites.module_kind: shared public static utility in the root package (enshrined\svgSanitize\Helper), one namespace away from the resolver

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/Helper.php:10-19 (Helper::getElementHref, a public static accessor in the root package that four call sites in two layers depend on)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is written about one predicate inside Resolver::processReferences, so the shared Helper accessor can be treated as that resolver's private detail, and the mixed-case <USE> element name, the mixed-case target ID and a percent-escaped fragment can each be argued to be invalid SVG or a browser/URL-parser quirk rather than the advisory's subject.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Mixed-case but safe hrefs must survive and be canonicalised (HrEf="#test3" becomes href="#test3"), and <use> elements whose href resolves to nothing must be kept rather than deleted; the fix's own added test for an unbound XLINK: prefix expects such <use> leftovers to remain. A fix that deletes every <use> whose attribute name is not exactly href/xlink:href, or that strips all <use> without a resolvable target, breaks this.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: src/Sanitizer.php:495-511; expectations in tests/data/hrefCleanOne.svg:1-12 and tests/SanitizerTest.php:122-132

O6_input_shapes: unprefixed mixed-case attribute name: HrEf, HREF
namespaced mixed-case local name: xlink:HrEf, xlink:HREF
<use> with no href attribute at all (the predicate is removed, so every <use> is inspected and then skipped at src/ElementReference/Resolver.php:111-113)
mixed-case unbound prefix XLINK:href, which must lose the reference rather than gain one

O7_producer.where: src/Sanitizer.php:487-511 — Sanitizer::cleanHrefAttributes() renames any case variant of href/xlink:href to the canonical name at src/Sanitizer.php:504-510, after the reference graph was built at src/Sanitizer.php:246

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Mixed-case target attribute ID/Id is never collected as a subject, because collectIdentifiedElements queries '//*[@id]' and Subject::getElementId reads getAttribute('id'); the <use> edges are invisible to the nesting and threshold checks while cleanAttributesOnWhitelist keeps the mixed-case name and an HTML parser lowercases it to a live id.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory and the fix are about the href attribute of <use>; id is never normalised anywhere in this library and XML ids are case-sensitive, so a mixed-case ID looks like invalid input rather than a reference the graph must count.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same class as the landing point, 15 lines above it

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A mixed-case element name <USE> is still not matched by the case-sensitive XPath node test after the fix, even though startClean treats tag names case-insensitively for the whitelist and for the use checks, so a mixed-case nesting bomb stays out of the graph and is emitted intact.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory speaks only of attribute names, and SVG element names are case-sensitive in XML, so <USE> reads as malformed input that no consumer would expand.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: landing file itself (the node-name test on the line above the fixed predicate)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A percent-encoded fragment href="#%61" is compared as the opaque id '%61' by extractIdReferenceFromHref, so the graph adds no edge for a reference a URL parser resolves to id 'a'; isHrefSafeValue allows it because it starts with '#'.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Fragment decoding is a URL-parser detail and the library documents hrefs as opaque strings that only need a literal leading '#', so decoding can be called the consumer's job.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: root package, one file from the landing point; different mechanism (identity parsing, not case sensitivity)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: isUseTagDirty reads $element->getAttribute('href') directly instead of going through Helper::getElementHref, so the per-element dirty check keeps a second, case-sensitive href accessor.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: a maintainer trimming a helper call out of the hot per-<use> loop would write exactly this, and it stays green against every canonical-attribute fixture in tests/data.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A private id-normalising accessor (case-insensitive id/ID lookup) added on Subject while the href side is being fixed, used by getElementId but not by the resolver's subject collection.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the id side of the same graph is adjacent to the file being fixed, and normalising on the accessor only looks like the minimal symmetric change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second node-name/query helper that matches a tag or attribute local name case-insensitively, used only for <use>, while collectIdentifiedElements keeps its '//*[@id]' query.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the element-name half of the same case problem most naturally lands in createNodeName, and a maintainer would add it there rather than touch the id query.

O9_family: improper handling of case sensitivity in a reference graph (CWE-178) leading to uncontrolled resource consumption (CWE-400) through <use> nesting/expansion

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Remove the '[@href or @xlink:href]' predicate (or inline a case-insensitive href read inside Resolver::processReferences) and stop there, leaving Helper::getElementHref, the mixed-case <USE>/ID spellings and the fragment-decoding differential untouched.
